description: Evidence-backed public claims ledger. Every claim carries a maturity (available | deployed-not-available | in-build | planned | vision), repo evidence, and vetted safe wording. check-ontology validates shape, evidence paths, and that `available` claims map to entities whose capability availability is complete. Marketing prose lives here, never in the semantic core.

claims.claim: Communities document regenerative work offline and sync when connectivity returns.
claims.safe_wording: The app works offline; queued work syncs automatically for passkey accounts and after a confirmation step for external wallets.

claims.claim: Field work becomes a permanent on-chain record at submission — or the moment it syncs, when captured offline.
claims.safe_wording: Work is attested on-chain at submission (offline submissions attest when the queue syncs); operator approval adds a separate linked approval attestation with confidence and verification method.

claims.claim: Gardeners sign in with a passkey — no seed phrase, no wallet setup.
claims.safe_wording: Passkey sign-in creates a smart account; common gardener flows are sponsored (gasless), while external-wallet operators may pay network gas.

claims.claim: Operator approval is what turns submitted work into verified impact — recorded with a confidence band and verification method.
claims.safe_wording: Operators — not evaluators — approve or reject submissions, writing confidence and verification method permanently on-chain. Approval gates verified impact; a decision is not guaranteed for every submission (actions can expire unreviewed).

claims.claim: Funders endow gardens: principal stays put while yield funds operations.
claims.safe_wording: Vault deposits, withdrawals, and yield harvests are live on Arbitrum One.

claims.claim: Gardens carry small rule-bound operational funds with capped, interval-limited withdrawals.
claims.safe_wording: Garden jars are provisioned automatically at garden mint; jar activity beyond creation is not yet indexed, so it does not appear in reports.

claims.claim: Gardeners claim recognition badges for milestones like their first submitted work.
claims.safe_wording: GreenWill badges are live on Arbitrum with an in-app claim flow (genesis, first submitted work, first support) — the contract validates the Work attestation, not its approval.

claims.claim: Approved work rolls up into fundable impact certificates.
claims.safe_wording: Operators mint Hypercert impact certificates from approved work; marketplace listing exists, and buyer-side flows are still maturing.

claims.claim: Gardeners can submit work through a Telegram bot.
claims.safe_wording: Telegram work submission is live; reviewing submission status happens in the app, not the bot. SMS and WhatsApp are direction, not shipped — never present them as current.

claims.claim: Commitment pooling is live on Arbitrum: gardens can register pools of promises on-chain.
claims.safe_wording: The commitment pooling contracts are deployed and unpaused on Arbitrum with 18 pools registered; the in-app experience is still rolling out, so nothing is user-facing yet. A commitment is a record, never a coin.

claims.claim: Fulfilled commitments settle in G$ through a cross-chain payout plan.
claims.safe_wording: Settlement contracts are deployed but paused with no value authority; G$ never bridges — an Arbitrum command executes on Celo with an authenticated acknowledgment. No value moves today.

claims.claim: Gardens can record interest-free advances and repayments against future work.
claims.safe_wording: The CreditRegistry is a records-only control plane — it never holds or transfers funds, and there is no credit score, ever. Deployed, not yet in use.

claims.claim: Communities will record Needs — problems paired with desired outcomes — that promises and funding can answer.
claims.safe_wording: Needs are a locked architecture (four EAS schemas, two resolvers) with implementation not started; nothing is deployed or user-visible yet.

claims.claim: Communities signal priorities continuously through conviction voting.
claims.safe_wording: The Gardens V2 module is deployed, but signal-pool creation needs an initialized community — describe governance chain-readiness as in progress, not live.

claims.claim: Green Goods is the field-operations layer of a full regenerative coordination stack.
claims.safe_wording: Present the full-stack framing as direction; the shipped product is offline-first documentation, verification, and funding rails on Arbitrum.
